findings.summary: The reported generation-2 failure is still not fixed; the change is provably inert there. prior_generation_state_roots(run_root, 2) builds pairs=[(1, dev_root/'state')] and range(2,2) is empty, so at generation 2 there is exactly ONE prior state root; _candidate_plans therefore produces at most one plan and the new review-depth-first `sorted` reduces to the identity. _walk's termination conditions are unchanged from the rejected attempt (chain-end at dd_replay.py:347, broken review link at 352, non-APPROVE at 369, missing continuous intent at 377). Since the incident proves g1's reviews were not replayable by _walk, generation 2 of dev-fg-31b963659d16 replays [configure, implement] exactly as before and materializes a fresh continuous review -- the same ORDER_VIOLATION. The new mechanism can only bite when a DIFFERENT prior generation holds the reviews, i.e. generation 3+, so spec requirement 3 is unmet for the sequence the spec actually reports.

A replayed candidate whose prefix ends at implement still opens a new feedback attempt, violating requirements 2 and 3. When the continuous receipt is absent, its link is broken, or its frozen intent is missing, _walk returns [configure, implement] and the pipeline dispatches and materializes a real continuous review on the replayed implement. With the inherited index ending in APPROVE (the reported condition, and the state of the committed index here), the carrier refuses it as 'a new attempt requires a prior REJECT'. Nothing in the change recognizes idempotent cross-generation replay from stable attempt/handoff/receipt identity as requirement 2 demands -- the pinned-attempt-id mechanism at dd_pipeline.py:417 predates this work and does not prevent the carrier from computing a new attempt. Two tests pin this failing behaviour as intended: test_a_review_whose_intent_is_missing_reruns_for_real (tests/test_dd_replay.py:357) and test_a_chain_broken_at_the_review_link_reruns_the_review (tests/test_dd_replay.py:405).

Requirement 5's mandated reproduction is still asserted only by proxy. test_a_fully_reviewed_chain_replays_through_to_acceptance builds a single prior generation with fully sealed reviews and intents, so _walk returns all four steps and the test passes identically without the _candidate_plans change -- it is not a regression test for this fix. No test anywhere asserts requirement 5's 'continuous-review handoff materialization succeeds': in this test no continuous-review handoff is materialized at all. The new TestTheFeedbackCarrierOrdering asserts against carrier_append (tests/test_dd_replay.py:185), a reimplementation of the plugin's rule defined in the test file itself, so it exercises the test helper rather than any product code and cannot detect a weakening of the real rule. test_the_review_bearing_prefix_is_preferred_over_a_partial_one asserts only on _build_plan and never reaches a review or acceptance boundary.

The new _select fallback loop can retry _prepare on a later candidate after an earlier candidate has already mutated the workspace, with no rollback. _prepare force-pushes the remote (dd_replay.py:584) and then `git reset --hard` (dd_replay.py:593) before installing receipts; if the reset fails, or an OSError is raised during receipt installation or _rewrite_run_config, _select catches it and moves to the next candidate against a tree/remote already moved to the first candidate's tip, leaving that candidate's partially installed receipt bytes in this generation's state root. _prepare documents itself as 'the one mutation', which the fallback no longer guarantees.

_build_plan is retained in product code but has no product caller; its only reference is tests/test_dd_replay.py:554. The candidate-preference behaviour it exposes is therefore asserted only through a private accessor that production never exercises.

Product-tree identity between 37c292ef and 582c318c could not be mechanically verified: this reviewer has only Read/Grep/Glob file inspection, so the mandated `git diff --exit-code ... ':(exclude).dev-dispatch'` was not executed and no shell or git command was run. File inspection of the worktree shows the .dev-dispatch/ namespace carrying the review artifacts and no sign of product drift, consistent with a compliant metadata-only materialization. Separately, the committed implement handoff records work_head_commit d9eab8dc29d47688de3eb57bc28b891dd8af9d69 while the review context supplies 37c292efbe437e472622d6e33fa8dae640540947 as the product commit -- consistent with a metadata-only implement materialization stacked on d9eab8dc, but unconfirmed against the object graph. Recorded for the deterministic seal, which verifies HEAD independently; not counted toward the REJECT.
